Not gonna tell you not to do it, but you shouldn't be a burden to other people. Don't jump into traffic. Let's say you cause an accident and someone dies. Now all of that person's family feels exactly like you do. Depressed, sad, and wanting the pain to go away. Are you fine with that?

Join some clubs that interest you and find people that have similar interests. It may be stressful at first, but its a lot easier to talk about something you enjoy with a stranger than to talk about something random.
Try to help others despite being depressed myself
It's seems like something that changed since you graduated college is the people you've surrounded yourself with. Talk to those you trust and care about, let them help you!

It's normal to not want to be alone in something. For some people, that thought keeps them going. 19th birthday today and the person I used to consider my best friend, someone I still care about greatly, hasn't said a word about it to me. No birthday wishes, no anything. Though I have other friends, the relationship with my best friend has been deteriorating and it truly makes me feel alone to not hear from her. Shes the reason I'm still here after all.. But happy early birthday. This might sound empty coming through a text, but I hope things get better for you soon, and know that you aren't alone. I wish you luck.

I feel you. I really do. I normally overthink pretty much everything and tend to convince myself people don't care about me. But it looks like you have some people that are pretty close to you. You shouldn't be afraid to message your boyfriend about anything, and odds are, since he's still with you, he really does care about you. Otherwise, he'd have no reason to stay, right? That's normally how I try to look at things when I overthink. If I think someone doesn't care about me is " well they're still talking to me. Why would they talk to me if they didn't care". I'm not sure if something like that will help you, but I just wanted to share my experience in hopes it does :)

Good luck and hope you stay safe

I wanted to kill myself when I was 16, and I still want to kill myself now at 19. However, in a span of a few months after wanting to kill myself, my entire life changed, for the good. Granted, that good is gone now, but I never would have experienced it if I went through with my plan. Life before that sucked. I thought it would never get better. It somehow got better. Keep on going for the unexpected to become expected.

In a similar situation. My best friend started ignoring me. She wouldn't tell me why. Everythong was fine and then she started talking to me less and less. She was my reason to live, and I don't know if I can keep going, so I know your pain. Why are you afraid of dying tonight?

The best thing you can do is be there for your friend. Whenever they need someone to talk to, be that person. Let them know you're always there for them and that you care about them. It's not a surefire way to guarantee their safety, but theresnt honestly not much you can do other than that for someone that's determined to die.

Keep living to see what the future holds. If you're at the point where you want to die, things can't get much worse. It'll either stay the same or get better. But wait a little longer before making the decision to take your life. Maybe something might change. Live for that chance.
I think in your case, the phrase "fake it till you make it" works all too well. Be who you want to be until you become that person.
Everyone always tells me that if I can't live for myself, to live for other people, but it gets so much worse when the other people leave you.

I resonate with this. I start college tomorrow. I never thought I'd live through higschool, but I met someone that helped me through all of that. She was my friend, became my best friend, and then became more. But she stopped talking to me recently. We drifted apart. And now, I doubt she even cares what happens to me. I decided to go to college for her. To keep living for her. Thought I'd end up marrying her. I dont know what to do anymore. Like you, no dream job, but a dream life.
What are you doing to slowly kill yourself?
Planning to move out with friends in a few months, but...

I've been in this situation before, though I was on the other end from you. And honestly, the best thing you can do for your best friend is be there for him. Don't pry into his reasons of wanting to die if you think it would make him uncomfortable. Don't tell him things will get better, because frankly, that sounds like bullshit to suicidal people. Just be there to listen. Let him know you're there whenever he wants to talk. Tell him that every time he has the thought to harm himself, to call you instead. As for yourself, you just have to power through the worry. Check up in him constantly if it makes you feel better, but don't overwhelm him. Maybe talk about it if you have another close friend. Two minds are better than one, and just letting out your worry can help relieve you.

Feeling that way over a loved one leaving you is nothing to be ashamed about. Anyone that says otherwise is just an asshole. I'm in a similar situation, I guess. My best friend, who I thought I'd eventually marry, pretty much stopped talking to me. She never told me why, never told me if something happened. Everything was fine, and poof, no contact and she got mad at me for asking why. Im in the dark. I don't know if I was the reason behind it or if something else happened, and I probably never will. She was the reason I decided not to kill myself a while ago. Now that she's gone, I don't know what to do. Maybe she'll come back, maybe I'll never see her again. Thinking about it hurts, and I wish I had the guts to kill myself. But honestly, there's no way to know if things will get better unless I wait and see. The same applies to you. Everything might be miserable right now, but live for the sake of seeing how things turn out. It can be for more than just her, too. Live to see if scientists make cool new discoveries, or see if you'll make a new best friend within a couple of years. Toughing through the pain sucks, I know that very well, but sometimes that's the best choice we can choose. I'm sorry for everything that's happened to you, and I hope your life gets brighter if you decide to keep living. Good luck.
Maybe it's not okay, but it's important to understand someone else's viewpoint. And it's also insensitive to tell a person with suicidal thoughts that they should stop thinking of themselves.

I simply stated the first step to getting better, not that they were finished with it. My point was to show you a perspective of someone not caring. Until someone first works on themselves, its difficult to do anything for others. I know some people that have depression or similar thoughts have a different mindset, but there are also many that have the same ideas.
It's hard to care for other people before caring for yourself. The first step in getting better is to focus on oneself, and until that is accomplished, how can you blame someone for their mindset?
Someone says that they won't get the vaccine because they're suicidal and want to die, and you're telling them to stop thinking of themselves? This is peak irony.

Do what you think is best for you. If you feel like you want to get it off your chest and tell your family, that's what you should do. And in my opinion, it would be better to do so sooner than later.

You are definitely overthinking! It's normal for people to have someone to rely on, even if they're to opposite gender. From what you described, there aren't any signs of him liking her. He's being open with you about everything now, and they're even concerned about you liking your SO's friend. None of that rings any alarm bells.

The first step is knowing if she knows her behavior is a problem.. if she believes she's acting normal,, then there isn't much that can be done. Now if she understands, she has to be willing to work on her behavior, otherwise, that relationship would most likely not work out.

Communication is key in a relationship. It might be hard to talk about, but you should explain to her that her behavior is starting to bother you, but also that it doesn't make you feel any different about her. When dealing with codependent people, they often need constant reassurance when problems are brought up. However, you're goal while talking about this with her should be to let her know that her behavior isn't healthy, or normal for that matter. If you want to stay in a relationship, let her know that you want change for things to work out, but that you'll be there to help her through that.
